messages:
Maria: hey folks — landing in Dublin Thursday morning, staying near Grand Canal. Quick Qs: best way from airport with a small suitcase? need a travel adapter? rain survival tips? :umbrella:
Kevin: Aircoach is super easy and roomy for luggage, or the 747/757 bus if it matches your stop. Taxis rank up but are fine if you're tired. Free Now app works here. Contactless cards accepted in most places.
Sasha: yup, Aircoach or a licensed taxi. If hotel is central LUAS tram is handy too. Also — bring a small foldable umbrella and a light waterproof layer. Layers > single heavy coat.
Ben: adapter = Type G (UK-style 3-rect pins). Hotels sometimes have them but don’t rely on it. If you need multiple plugs bring a small adapter with USB ports.
Liz: pro tip: download Google Maps offline for the area and screenshot key confirmation codes. Avoid Temple Bar for dinner unless you want tourist prices; try Stoneybatter or Capel Street for better food. :pizza:
Maria: any recs for a short-term SIM/eSIM? i don't want to deal with stores after landing.
Kevin: Airalo eSIM worked well for me last time — instant install. Otherwise Vodafone/Three kiosks at the airport. But most places have good Wi‑Fi.
Sasha: for transit consider a Leap Visitor Card if you plan to use bus/tram a lot. Otherwise contactless payment on buses/trams is convenient. LUAS stops are a few blocks from Grand Canal spots.
Ben: packing cheats (carry-on only):
```
- Type G adapter (1)
- packable rain jacket
- thin merino layer
- waterproof sneakers
- small umbrella
- power bank + USB-C cable
- travel-size toiletries in 100ml bottles
```
Liz: also slip on shoes make airport security faster. Shoe bags / shower caps save suitcase cleanliness. And if you want a nice pint without the tourists, ask locals for pubs in Smithfield area. :beers:
Maria: perfect — thanks!! flying carry-on only so those packing tips are clutch. see you at the offsite 🙌
